findings.evidence: `pkg/executor/sortexec/sort.go:780-787` builds `keyCmpFuncs` for every `ByItems` entry, while `pkg/executor/sortexec/sort.go:791-803` skips `*expression.Constant` when building `keyColumns`. Comparators then index `keyCmpFuncs[i]` + `ByItems[i].Desc` by the *position in `keyColumns`* (`pkg/executor/sortexec/sort.go:806-816`), assuming all three slices stay aligned. The same positional assumption exists in partition sorting (`pkg/executor/sortexec/sort_partition.go:274-289`) and TopN heap ordering (`pkg/executor/sortexec/topn.go:153-165`). The added regression test explicitly disables `column_prune` and runs cases where the constant is not trailing (e.g. `order by -646041453, c` in `pkg/executor/sortexec/parallel_sort_test.go:157-193`), making misalignment reachable. `chunk.CompareFunc` requires same-typed columns (`pkg/util/chunk/compare.go:26-43`); if the misaligned compare func is a string compare, it calls `Column.GetString` which uses `offsets` (`pkg/util/chunk/column.go:641-643`) and will panic on fixed-len columns (e.g., INT).
findings.fix: Make the “ignored constant” handling keep comparator state aligned: build and use aligned slices for only the effective sort keys, e.g. `{colIdx, cmpFunc, desc}` per key, or keep a mapping from `keyColumns` positions back to the original `ByItems` index. Concretely: while building keys, append `col.Index`, `chunk.GetCompareFunc(col.RetType)`, and `by.Desc` together for `*expression.Column`; skip constants by skipping *all* three; then update `lessRow`/`compareRow`/`greaterRow` and `sortPartition` to use the aligned `desc` slice (not `e.ByItems[i].Desc` / `byItemsDesc[i]`).
findings.impact: When optimizer rule `column_prune` is disabled (supported via `mysql.opt_rule_blacklist` as used in the regression test), ORDER BY lists can include constants in arbitrary positions. With the current implementation, non-trailing constants can cause: (1) wrong ORDER BY direction (e.g. `ORDER BY 1 DESC, c ASC` becomes effectively `c DESC` due to `Desc` misalignment), affecting LIMIT/TopN row selection; and/or (2) runtime panics from type-mismatched compare funcs (e.g. `ORDER BY 'x', c_int`) because the compare func chosen from the constant is applied to a different column type.
findings.later_fix_evidence: Checked `upstream/master:pkg/executor/sortexec/sort.go` and it still has the same `buildKeyColumns()` constant-skip logic and the same positional indexing in `lessRow()` (no mapping / aligned desc slice), so this issue is not fixed later on `upstream/master`.
findings.verify: Extend `TestIssue55344` (with `column_prune` still blacklisted) to include cases that would expose misalignment: `order by 1 desc, c asc`, `order by 'x', c`, and a mixed-type constant before a fixed-len column; also add a TopN/LIMIT variant to validate correct row selection. Run `go test ./pkg/executor/sortexec -run TestIssue55344` and ensure no panic and correct ordering.
findings.what: Sort/TopN key construction skips constant BY items without also filtering/re-aligning `keyCmpFuncs` and `Desc` flags, so comparisons can use the wrong compare func / sort direction whenever a constant ORDER BY item is not trailing.

subject: executor: fix query hang when sorted column is constant (#55418)
summary: Commit fixes hang paths by closing channels on early errors and adds coverage for ORDER BY constants with column_prune disabled. However, the constant-skip implementation can misalign sort key metadata (cmp funcs/desc vs column indexes), leading to wrong ordering or panics in reachable scenarios.
